parameters.content:
## Stage 1 – Topic → Video Ideas
Reads existing titles (avoids repeats), Gemini generates ideas, code adds VID-IDs, saves to **Video Ideas**, picks the Selected idea.

## Stage 2 – Research
Gemini builds a research plan for the selected idea → **Content Research** sheet.

## Stage 3 – Script
Idea + research → Gemini writes script (uses only provided research, [VERIFY] flags) → **Scripts** sheet.

## Stage 4 – Publishing Data
Title options, description, tags, summary, chapters → **Publishing Data** sheet.

## Stage 5 – Thumbnail Plan
Concept, text, visual description, image prompt → **Thumbnails** sheet.

## Stage 6 – Content Calendar
Builds calendar row (Status: Production) → **Content Calendar**.

## Stage 7 – Simulated Metrics
Generates simulated (clearly labelled) views/CTR/watch time → **Video Performance**.

## Stage 8 – Mark Published
Updates the calendar row to Published.

## Stage 9 – AI Performance Report
Code computes metrics; Gemini only interprets them with evidence → **Analytics Reports**.

# Beginner AI Lab – Complete YouTube Pipeline
Manual run: Topic → Ideas → Research → Script → Publishing Data → Thumbnail → Calendar → Metrics → Published → AI Report. Database: Google Sheets. AI: Gemini.

assignments.name: audience
assignments.value: Students and beginners with no technical background

parameters.text:
=You are a YouTube content strategist for a fictional channel called "{{ $json.channel_name }}".
The channel teaches {{ $json.channel_topic }} to: {{ $json.audience }}.

Generate {{ $json.idea_count }} original YouTube video ideas for BEGINNERS.

For each idea provide:
- title: a clear, beginner-friendly video title
- topic: the broad subject (e.g. AI Tools, AI Basics, Productivity, Automation)
- category: one of Tutorial, Explainer, Comparison, Productivity, Education
- explanation: 1 to 2 sentences on what the video covers and why it is useful
- target_audience: who this specific video is for
- priority: High, Medium or Low

Rules:
- Ideas must be original, practical and realistic. Do not make unsupported claims.
- Do not use real brand logos, real channel names or copyrighted content.
- Do NOT repeat any of these existing titles: {{ $json.existing_titles }}

Return only the structured data.

parameters.jsCode:
const rows = $('Format Rows and Create IDs').all().map(i => i.json);
return [{ json: rows.find(r => r['Status'] === 'Selected') || rows[0] }];

parameters.text:
=You are a YouTube content researcher for a fictional beginner-focused channel called "Beginner AI Lab".
The audience is students and beginners with no technical background.

Create a research and content plan for this video idea:

Title: {{ $json['Title'] }}
Topic: {{ $json['Topic'] }}
Category: {{ $json['Category'] }}
Target audience: {{ $json['Target Audience'] }}
Idea summary: {{ $json['Explanation'] }}

Provide:
- learning_goal: 1 to 2 sentences on what the viewer should learn or be able to do after watching
- main_points: 4 to 6 key points the video must cover
- viewer_questions: 4 to 6 questions beginners are likely to ask about this topic
- intro: a short description of how the video should open and hook the viewer
- main_content: a short description of the main teaching section, in order
- examples: 2 to 3 simple, practical examples to show on screen
- conclusion: a short description of how to wrap up and what to tell viewers to do next
- verify_before_publishing: facts, features, prices, limits or claims that must be checked before publishing

Rules:
- Use plain, beginner-friendly language.
- Do not invent statistics, prices, or product features. If something may have changed or you are unsure, list it under verify_before_publishing.
- Do not use real logos, real channel names or copyrighted content.

Return only the structured data.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample:
{
  "learning_goal": "Viewers learn how to write clear prompts that give better AI answers.",
  "main_points": ["Point one", "Point two", "Point three", "Point four"],
  "viewer_questions": ["Question one?", "Question two?", "Question three?", "Question four?"],
  "intro": "Open with a relatable problem, then promise a simple fix.",
  "main_content": "Walk through the steps in order, with one demo per step.",
  "examples": ["Example one", "Example two"],
  "conclusion": "Recap the key steps and invite viewers to try one prompt today.",
  "verify_before_publishing": ["Check any tool features or limits mentioned"]
}

{
  "hook": "Ever asked an AI a question and got a useless answer? Stay with me, because in the next five minutes you will fix that.",
  "script": "HOOK
...

SECTION 1: ...
...

CONCLUSION
...

CALL TO ACTION
...",
  "call_to_action": "If this helped, subscribe and watch our next video on writing better prompts."
}

parameters.text:
=You are a YouTube publishing specialist for a fictional beginner-focused channel called "Beginner AI Lab".
Tone: clear, friendly and honest. Audience: students and beginners.

Create the publishing information for this video, based ONLY on the script below.

Working title: {{ $json['Title'] }}

SCRIPT:
{{ $json['Script'] }}

Provide:
- title_options: exactly 5 different YouTube titles. Each must be clear, relevant to what the video really covers, and under 70 characters.
- recommended_title: the best one of the five (copy it exactly)
- title_reason: one sentence explaining why it fits the video's actual content
- description: a YouTube description of 80 to 150 words. First 2 sentences should summarize the video and make viewers want to watch. Include a natural call to action to subscribe. No links.
- tags: 10 to 15 relevant keywords or short phrases
- summary: a 2 to 3 sentence summary of the video
- chapters: one short chapter title for EACH script section, in the same order as the script (HOOK, each SECTION, CONCLUSION, CALL TO ACTION). Use 2 to 5 words each.

Rules:
- Use only what is in the script. Do not invent statistics, prices, results or product features.
- No clickbait or exaggerated promises (avoid words like "ultimate", "guaranteed", "secret", "shocking" unless the script supports them).
- Do not use real logos, real channel names or copyrighted content.
- Keep any [VERIFY] items out of the title and description. Do not state them as facts.

Return only the structured data.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample:
{
  "title_options": [
    "AI for Beginners: What It Is and How It Works",
    "What Is AI? A Simple Guide for Beginners",
    "How Does AI Work? Explained Without Jargon",
    "AI Explained Simply: Start Here",
    "Understanding AI: A Beginner's Walkthrough"
  ],
  "recommended_title": "AI for Beginners: What It Is and How It Works",
  "title_reason": "It names the exact topic and audience covered in the script.",
  "description": "In this video, we explain what AI is in simple language...",
  "tags": ["AI for beginners", "what is AI", "how AI works", "AI explained"],
  "summary": "A simple introduction to AI for people with no technical background.",
  "chapters": ["Intro", "What AI is", "How AI learns", "Everyday examples", "Recap", "Next steps"]
}

parameters.text:
=You are a thumbnail designer for a fictional beginner-focused YouTube channel called "Beginner AI Lab".
Style: clean, friendly, high contrast, easy to read on a phone. Audience: students and beginners.

Create a thumbnail plan for this video.

Title: {{ $json['Recommended Title'] }}
Summary: {{ $json['Summary'] }}

Provide:
- concept: one sentence describing the thumbnail idea
- thumbnail_text: 2 to 4 words of large, readable text. It must match the video and not promise anything the video does not cover
- visual_description: 2 to 4 sentences describing exactly what appears (main subject, background, colours, where the text sits, what is in the foreground)
- image_prompt: a single detailed prompt for an AI image generator, 16:9 widescreen, that includes the style, subject, background, colour palette and "empty space on one side for text". Do not ask the image tool to render text
- visual_assets_needed: 3 to 5 other visual assets the video will need (for example screen recordings, simple diagrams, icons, b-roll ideas)

Rules:
- No real brand logos, product logos, app icons or named AI products (do not show the logo of any AI tool).
- No copyrighted characters, celebrities, real people or real channel names.
- Use generic, original visuals only, such as a friendly robot made of simple shapes, a laptop, a lightbulb, a notebook or abstract shapes.
- No clickbait, fake numbers or exaggerated claims in the text.

Return only the structured data.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample:
{
  "concept": "A friendly simple robot beside a glowing lightbulb to show AI made easy.",
  "thumbnail_text": "AI MADE SIMPLE",
  "visual_description": "A flat-style friendly robot made of rounded shapes stands on the right. A large lightbulb glows beside it. The background is a clean blue gradient with empty space on the left for bold text.",
  "image_prompt": "Flat vector illustration, friendly small robot made of simple rounded shapes, glowing lightbulb, clean blue and yellow palette, soft gradient background, empty space on the left side for text, 16:9 widescreen, no text, no logos",
  "visual_assets_needed": ["Screen recording of a chat tool", "Simple diagram of how AI learns", "Lightbulb icon", "Notebook b-roll"]
}

parameters.text:
=You are a YouTube analytics assistant for a fictional beginner-focused channel called "Beginner AI Lab".

IMPORTANT: All data below is SIMULATED, fictional test data. Treat every result as simulated, never as real audience behaviour.

PERFORMANCE DATA (already calculated, use only these numbers):
{{ $json.stats_json }}

Write a report with:
- overall_summary: 2 to 3 sentences on overall simulated performance
- higher_engagement_topics: topics or categories with higher simulated engagement
- lower_engagement_topics: topics or categories with lower simulated engagement
- video_summaries: one short summary for EVERY video in the data (video_id and summary)
- suggested_topics: 5 future video ideas based on the simulated patterns
- improvements: 3 to 5 possible areas for improvement
- data_note: one sentence stating the results are simulated

Rules:
- Use ONLY the numbers provided. Do not invent figures, trends, dates or causes.
- Every item in the topic lists, suggested_topics and improvements must include an "evidence" field quoting the specific metric (for example "avg engagement 11.1% vs overall 8.9%").
- Be cautious: use words like "may" and "suggests". Do not state causes as facts.
- If a group has low_sample = true, say the sample is small and do not draw firm conclusions from it.
- Suggested topics must be original and beginner-friendly, with no real brands or copyrighted content.

Return only the structured data.
